exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: Strong growth-lab work reads its own equation like a story — here is how one student modeled a savings jar.

traits.trait: Defines both variables and the equation
traits.sample: My equation is s = 15w: w is weeks and s is the predicted subscriber total, assuming exactly 15 new subscribers every week.
traits.why: The variables, direction of dependence, and constant-rate assumption are explicit.

traits.sample: The point (0, 0) means at week zero I had saved nothing — my line must start there because saving is proportional.
traits.why: The graph feature is interpreted in context, not just plotted.

traits.sample: If I saved $30 a week instead, the line would climb twice as steeply — same start, double the rise per week.
traits.why: It links the constant k to the visual slope of the line.

traits.sample: To reach $180 I solved 180 = 15w, so w = 12 weeks — the table and the graph agree at (12, 180).
traits.why: The milestone is verified three ways: equation, table, graph.
